content: JWT tokens must include an exp claim for expiry validation; tokens without expiry are rejected by the auth middleware.
Rotating JWT signing keys requires a grace window where both old and new keys validate to avoid mid-flight session breakage.
User sessions are stored in Redis with a 24-hour TTL and refreshed on each authenticated request.
Cache invalidation in Redis uses pub/sub channels keyed by entity type so all app instances drop stale entries simultaneously.
Pipelining Redis commands cuts round-trip latency by 5-10x on bulk operations; never issue thousands of single GETs in a loop.
Payment processing must use idempotency keys on every charge; without them, network retries cause duplicate charges and chargebacks.
Stripe webhook payloads must be HMAC-verified using the signing secret before any side effect; never trust the payload directly.
The TDD cycle is red (failing test), green (minimal pass), refactor (clean up). Skipping red means you can't prove the test catches the bug.
The test pyramid puts unit tests at the base, integration tests in the middle, e2e at the top — invert it and CI times balloon.
Zero-downtime schema migrations require expand-contract: add nullable column, backfill, switch reads, drop old column in a later release.
Long-held migration locks block writes; set lock_timeout to a few seconds and retry rather than blocking production traffic.
Optimize the p95 latency, not the average. Averages hide tail behavior, and tail latency is what users perceive as slowness.
Flame graphs make CPU hotspots obvious; the widest stack frames are where you spend time, not where you think you spend it.
The YAMO kernel heartbeat monitors agent drift and triggers skill evolution when reliability drops below threshold.
YAMO audit blocks are batched into a SHA-256 Merkle tree and periodically anchored to maintain cryptographic provenance.
OAuth access tokens carry scopes that gate endpoint access; requesting overly broad scopes at consent time widens the blast radius when a token leaks.
Service API keys rotate quarterly via the secrets manager; deploys pick up the new key from the environment while the old key stays valid for 48 hours.
Passwords are hashed with argon2id (64MB memory, 3 iterations); bcrypt remains only for legacy rows and upgrades on the next successful login.
State-changing endpoints require a CSRF token bound to the session; pure JSON APIs behind bearer auth skip CSRF because browsers cannot set Authorization headers cross-origin.
Redis persistence uses AOF with everysec fsync; RDB snapshots alone can lose up to a full snapshot interval of writes on crash.
Memcached beats Redis for pure ephemeral caching at high concurrency, but offers no persistence, pub/sub, or rich data structures.
Static assets ship with immutable Cache-Control and content-hashed filenames; HTML gets no-store so deploys become visible immediately.
Refunds are issued against the original charge id, never as standalone transfers, so reconciliation ties every refund to its capture.
Money amounts are stored as integer minor units; floating-point rounding on currency is a compliance bug, not a style choice.
Failed subscription renewals enter dunning: retries at 1, 3, and 7 days with customer emails, then cancellation.
Every migration ships with a tested down() path; irreversible migrations require a data export step and sign-off before deploy.
Large backfills run as batched background jobs with rate limits, never inside the migration itself, to keep deploys fast.
Long garbage-collection pauses in Node surface as event-loop lag; monitor loop delay and heap growth rather than CPU utilization alone.
Database connection pools should be sized near cores-times-two on the database server; oversized pools add contention, not throughput.
The N+1 query pattern is invisible on dev datasets; eager-load associations or batch with a dataloader before production scale exposes it.
Kafka guarantees ordering only within a partition; choose the partition key by the entity whose event order matters.
Consumer lag alerts fire on time-lag, not offset-lag; offset deltas are meaningless across topics with different throughput.
Messages that fail processing three times land in the dead-letter queue with the original payload and the last error attached.
Exactly-once delivery is a myth across process boundaries; build idempotent consumers and accept at-least-once semantics.
Rolling updates keep maxUnavailable at zero for user-facing services; surge pods absorb traffic while old pods drain.
Pods handle SIGTERM by failing readiness first, draining in-flight requests, then exiting before the grace period ends.
CPU limits cause throttling even at low utilization; set requests accurately and drop CPU limits for latency-sensitive services.
Risky changes ship dark behind feature flags; the flag lifecycle includes a removal ticket so dead flags do not accumulate.
Blue-green deploys swap the router between two identical environments; rollback is a router flip, not a redeploy.
Embedding dimension trades recall for storage; Matryoshka-trained models tolerate truncation to lower dimensions with modest quality loss.
IVF-PQ indexes trade exact recall for speed; below roughly ten thousand vectors a flat scan is both faster and exact.
Cross-encoder rerankers add hundreds of milliseconds; apply them to the top twenty candidates, never the full result set.
Chunk documents on semantic boundaries rather than fixed windows; mid-sentence splits poison both embedding quality and retrieval.
Hybrid retrieval fuses vector and BM25 rankings with reciprocal rank fusion; neither channel alone handles both paraphrase and exact-identifier queries.
Logs are structured JSON with a request id on every line; grep-able prose logs do not survive fan-out across services.
Head-based trace sampling at one percent loses the errors you care about; tail-based sampling keeps every trace containing an error span.
Every page must be actionable; alerts that auto-resolve or lack a runbook get deleted, not snoozed.
SLOs define an error budget; when the budget burns down, feature work pauses in favor of reliability work.
TypeScript strict mode pays for itself at refactor time; the any escape hatch concentrates bugs exactly where types were hardest to write.
ESM and CommonJS interop breaks at default exports; dual-publish packages need explicit exports maps tested from both module systems.
CI must install from the lockfile with npm ci; a floating install can silently test different dependency versions than production ships.
A flaky test is a failing test; quarantine it the day it flakes and fix or delete it within the sprint, because trust in the suite decays fast.
Property-based tests generate inputs to falsify invariants; they find edge cases that example-based tests never encode.
Prefer fakes over mocks for collaborators you own; mock-heavy suites verify call choreography instead of behavior.
SQL injection dies with parameterized queries; string-concatenated WHERE clauses are unacceptable even in internal tools.
Secrets live in the secrets manager, not in .env files committed to repos; local development uses developer-scoped short-lived credentials.
Dependency audits gate CI at high severity; transitive advisories with no exploit path get documented exceptions, not blanket ignores.
The YAMO decision context graph links memories with typed supersedes and contradicts edges so reversed decisions surface their dependents.
Synthesized YAMO skills stage in a quarantine directory until kappa approval commits them to the live skill path.
The YAMO route prior learns per-intent provider success rates from closed dispatches and overrides rule-based routing only with sufficient evidence.
